subject.title: Feature: Add denylist support for exec-approvals

question: What native exec-approvals denylist semantics should OpenClaw support for command/content matches under permissive or allowlist exec policies?
rationale: The request changes a security boundary and persisted config/protocol/UI behavior, and the open PRs propose materially different semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Review the direct denylist PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92456 as the main candidate and require protocol, prompt-parity, docs, upgrade, mergeability, and live approval proof before merge.

options.title: Land path-deny separately
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88075 as a narrower sensitive-path hardening track while keeping command/content denylist policy open here.

options.title: Reject native denylist mode
options.body: Close the direction only if maintainers decide allow-everything-except policies are outside OpenClaw's security model and should remain plugin or external policy-engine territory.

recommendation.title: Review the direct denylist PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92456 as the main candidate and require protocol, prompt-parity, docs, upgrade, mergeability, and live approval proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest explicit issue-review signal and already scoped this as a native security-policy decision across the affected surfaces.
